row.evidence: Backstage's framework and core features are open source and free to use; its catalog ingests users and teams from Microsoft Entra ID via the Microsoft Graph API (or from LDAP), and no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row for the open-source Backstage framework (CNCF project started by Spotify); it is free and self-hosted, so plan and price fields are null. No SCIM: status 'none' by absence. Identity comes from two pieces: auth providers (Okta OIDC, Microsoft, Google, generic OIDC and others) for sign-in, and catalog entity providers that pull users and groups on a schedule from Microsoft Entra ID (msgraph module) or LDAP/Active Directory. Those providers are recorded as directory sync (idp.entra = directory_sync). Spotify Portal for Backstage, the commercial SaaS version, is quote-only and its SSO/SCIM support was not documented on the pages read.

scim.notes: Backstage is a self-hosted open-source framework with no SCIM endpoint in its docs (backstage.io sitemap has no SCIM page). Users and groups enter the catalog through pull-based entity providers (Microsoft Graph, LDAP and others); sign-in uses auth providers with sign-in resolvers. Status 'none' by absence.

user_api.notes: Users are catalog entities (kind User) loaded from entity providers; no separate user-management API was researched.

okta.notes: OIN search for 'backstage' returns no results; Backstage ships its own Okta OIDC auth provider (c8).

entra.notes: No Entra gallery app; the open-source msgraph catalog module pulls users and groups from the tenant on a schedule.

fallbacks.other_sync: Catalog entity providers pull users and groups from Microsoft Entra ID (Microsoft Graph) and LDAP / Active Directory / FreeIPA on a schedule
fallbacks.notes: Sign-in resolvers map an external identity to a Backstage user; a matching catalog user entity is encouraged but not required.
